chunks: From him, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn and Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn ʿAli ibn Faddal, from his father, from ʿAli ibn ʿUqbah and Dhubyan ibn Hakim, from Musa ibn Ukayl, from ʿAmr ibn Shimr, from Jabir ibn Yazid, from Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

"What is upon any one of you, when he has buried his deceased, leveled the earth over him, and departed from his grave, except that he remain behind by it and then say: O so-and-so son of so-and-so, are you upon the covenant by which we knew you—namely the testimony that there is no god but Allah, that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and that ʿAli Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام is your Imam, and so-and-so and so-and-so—until he reaches the last of them? For when he does that, one of the two angels says to his companion: We have been spared reaching him and questioning him, for he has been instructed. So they turn away from him and do not enter upon him."

key_terms.الْعَهْدِ: the covenant or commitment of faith
key_terms.الْمَلَكَيْنِ: the two angels assigned to questioning
key_terms.لُقِّنَ: has been instructed or prompted with the creed

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about تلقين the deceased after burial?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the practice of تلقين after burial, in which the deceased is reminded of the testimony of faith, the Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, and the Imams عليهم السلام. It presents this as beneficial for the dead in the grave, indicating that such instruction affects the encounter with the questioning angels.
